text:
maria: FYI customer ran a client-side clip (seek forward then back) and we ended up charging the toolcall twice. logs attached, short thread. :grimacing:

sam: Oof. Any chance this is just a logging dupe vs real billing?

maria: I diffed ledger rows. Two distinct rows: one provisional at serve time, one confirmed after resume. Different run_id. Example log snippet:
```
[router] 2026-12-08T09:10:11Z session=sess-77 action=clip to=seq=120 from=seq=105 client_nonce=nonce-42
[runner] 2026-12-08T09:10:11Z run_id=run-abc invoked_tool=tally-tool out_tokens=24 provisional=true
[billing] 2026-12-08T09:10:12Z row_id=rb-555 amount=24 provisional=true key=run-abc
[router] 2026-12-08T09:10:13Z client_replay resume_seq=105 new_run=run-def
[billing] 2026-12-08T09:10:14Z row_id=rb-556 amount=24 provisional=false key=run-def
```

trent: so same logical tool call but different runtime key. Our dedupe is run-key based and not tied to a higher-level resume id.

olivia: console/ops request: surface "replay/clip" markers in the billing timeline + link to session trace so SRE/CS can see why invoice had duplicate entries.

sam: quick thought: if client sends a resume_nonce on seek/clip, router can attach resume_nonce to all subsequent tool invocations until next boundary. Billing should prefer resume_nonce when present for dedupe/promotion.

maria: Agree. Alternative: use a synthetic resume_token derived from session+client_nonce+payload_hash so server-generated resumes from trimming can still be correlated.

trent: DB concerns: changing idempotency key used by ledger is a migration with risk. We'll need migration that backfills recent provisional rows with resume_token=session or inferred token if client_nonce missing. Also add uniqueness constraint on (resume_token, tool_fingerprint) but that might conflict with older rows.

olivia: UX note: add a "billing reconciliation" toggle in the console that shows provisional vs confirmed and groups suspected duplicates by resume_token. That helps CS issues right away.

sam: short-term mitigation: when we see a resume within X seconds and payload hash matches, mark the second run as "suspect-duplicate" and emit a reconciliation alert instead of immediately finalizing billing. This buys time for human review.

maria: We must be careful: delaying finalization increases provisional time and could confuse customers. Add explicit TTL and auto-finalize after 30s if no promotion. Also expose metric billing.provisional_delay_seconds.

trent: instrumentation: emit event resume.detected={offset_diff, client_nonce_present, resume_token:<if any>} and billing.event={provisional_created, provisional_promoted, provisional_flagged_dup}. Add guardrails to revert the new dedupe if the false-negative rate is > 0.5% in first 24h of rollout.

olivia: I'll draft the console changes and a small customer-facing blurb explaining "You may see provisional duplicates during replay/clip operations; they are subject to reconciliation."

infra-bot: tango-checklist: add DB backfill job ticket infra/1342, add schema change ticket infra/1343, and a feature-flag for resume_token idempotency.

sam: Implementation plan (phased):
1) emit resume_token from router when client_nonce present or when we infer a seek/clip. carry through runner -> billing as optional idempotency key.
2) billing: if resume_token && match on (resume_token, tool_sig) then promote provisional instead of inserting duplicate. If no match, insert provisional as today.
3) add console grouping and telemetry counters.
4) run backfill to set resume_token=session for recent provisionals behind FF.

maria: I'll open eng-platform#4210 with repro + logs + customer context. Sam/Trent can PR the billing change behind FF. Olivia will own console UX.

trent: one extra edge: client-side retries where nonce changes but payload identical. We'll need a payload signature check to avoid undercharging. Proposed rule: resume_token match OR payload_sig match within short window => treat as same and annotate.

sam: Good call. We'll record payload_sig and compare with Levenshtein threshold? Maybe just strong hash of request body + model + tool flags. fuzzy compare is messy. Use sha256(payload) for now.

maria: ok. we have an action list. thanks team. :raised_hands:

infra-bot: created infra/1342, infra/1343, featureflag/resume-idemp."
